title: Safe Memory event
description: One thing that happened in GB's life, normalised from any source. Safe Memory answers what happened, what he has, what he watched, where he was. It never stores ideas: that is MindBase's half of the boundary (MindBase V6 Plan C2). The two cross-reference by id through project_ref.

id.description: ev-<group>-<suffix>. The real store writes ev-YYYYMMDD-<suffix>; the stub's fixture rows write ev-fixture-NNNN, which is the same shape and is impossible to mistake for a recorded event. Stable for the life of the event: a re-import of the same source row yields the same id.

kind.description: The closed kind vocabulary. A grant is written in these words, so adding one is a contract change, not an implementation detail.

source.description: Which connector produced the event. Present so a duplicate across sources (an Amazon order seen both in the export and in a Gmail receipt) can be reconciled rather than counted twice.

ts.description: ISO 8601 with offset, in the timezone the event happened in. Never UTC-normalised: 'what did I buy yesterday' is a local-day question.

title.description: What a person would call it. One line, no source boilerplate.

entities.description: Brands, people, channels, categories. The free-text search surface beyond the title.

amount.description: Minor units of `currency` (ARS centavos, USD cents). Integer on purpose: money is never a float here. Null when the kind carries no amount.

place.description: Reverse-geocoded place name. The only location field a redacted grant may see.

media_ref.description: Provider-native media identifier (a YouTube video id, a Photos UUID). Never a URL to a third party that would leak a read.

raw_ref.description: Pointer INTO the encrypted raw export that produced this event, as <relative path>#<row key>. The raw file never leaves the machine; this is how a claim is audited back to its origin.

project_ref.description: A MindBase project slug or mb-id this event belongs to. The one link across the boundary, and it is written by MindBase, never inferred here.

fixture.description: True only on rows served by the stub server from fixtures/. The real store never sets it, so nothing downstream can mistake a fixture for a recorded event.
